skill.name: faceswap
skill.description: Use the verging.ai API to swap a face into a short video from local files or supported remote URLs.
skill.summary: Creates AI face-swap videos through verging.ai with media upload, trimming, job polling, and optional result download.
skill.author: verging.ai

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate verging.ai face-swap workflow, but it performs real outbound network calls, external media processing commands, API-key handling, and temporary file storage. Many Markdown backtick findings are false positives, while the confirmed risks center on credential exposure in curl commands, third-party upload of biometric media, and arbitrary remote media inputs.

remediation.issue: Consent and impersonation controls are not enforced.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit consent checks, clear prohibited-use language, and refusal guidance for non-consensual, deceptive, or rights-infringing face swaps.

remediation.issue: Biometric media is uploaded to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose upload destinations, retention expectations, result URL visibility, and privacy impact before sending video or face images.

remediation.issue: API keys are passed through curl command-line headers.
remediation.suggestion: Use safer credential handling such as restricted config files, stdin-supported tooling, or runtime secret injection that avoids process-list exposure.

remediation.issue: Remote URLs are downloaded and parsed by local tools.
remediation.suggestion: Validate URL schemes, quote all paths, reject shell metacharacters in implementations, and confirm trusted sources before running yt-dlp, curl, ffprobe, or ffmpeg.

remediation.issue: Sensitive media is stored in a predictable /tmp directory.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mktemp, set restrictive permissions, and remove files automatically after completion or failure.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Non-Consensual Face Swap Misuse
semantic_findings.description: The skill accepts arbitrary video and face image inputs, then creates a face-swap job. It only reminds users to process media they have rights to, so misuse for impersonation or non-consensual synthetic media remains possible.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented options accept any video and face image path or URL, and the create-job step uploads the face image directly. The rights reminder is helpful but does not enforce consent.

semantic_findings.title: Biometric Media Sent to Third-Party Services
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uploads video and face images to verging.ai and storage URLs, then returns external result locations. This creates privacy exposure for biometric media beyond the local machine.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The upload and create-job steps explicitly transfer user media to remote API and storage endpoints. The response examples show externally hosted upload and result URLs.

content.value_statement: Face-swap video workflows need several upload, trim, and polling steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through the verging.ai API flow.
actual_capabilities: Accepts local video files or YouTube and Bilibili video URLs.
Accepts local face images or remote face image URLs.
Uses VERGING_API_KEY to authenticate with the verging.ai API.
Trims videos with ffmpeg and ffprobe to a 30 second maximum.
Uploads videos and face images through the documented multipart API workflow.
Polls job status and returns the result URL or downloads the final video.
limitations: Requires yt-dlp, ffmpeg, ffprobe, curl, and a valid verging.ai API key.
Sends uploaded video and face media to third-party processing services.
Uses verging.ai credits, with higher cost for HD output.
Does not enforce consent, identity verification, or watermarking.

use_cases.title: Prototype Short Face-Swap Clips
use_cases.description: Create short test clips from approved video and face assets while checking credits and API job status.

use_cases.title: Prepare Controlled Marketing Drafts
use_cases.description: Generate internal concept videos from licensed footage before sending approved assets to a production team.

use_cases.title: Automate Media API Workflows
use_cases.description: Combine trimming, upload, polling, and optional download into a repeatable command-line process.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Local Swap
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner use with local media files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use faceswap with ./video.mp4 and ./face.jpg. Keep normal quality and show me the result URL when the job finishes.

prompt_templates.title: Trim and Download the Result
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate use with a selected segment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use faceswap on ./source.mp4 and ./approved-face.jpg from 5 to 25 seconds. Download the completed result to ./outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Use Remote Video and Image Sources
prompt_templates.prompt: Use faceswap with this YouTube video URL and this face image URL. Confirm the duration before uploading media.

prompt_templates.title: Check Credits Before HD Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my verging.ai credits, estimate the HD cost for a 20 second clip, then run faceswap only if enough credits remain.

output_examples.input: A local video and local face image are provided with normal quality.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the clip duration, confirms credit needs, uploads the media, polls progress, and returns the completed result link.

output_examples.input: A 40 second source video is provided with a requested 10 to 25 second segment.
output_examples.output: The assistant trims the selected segment, creates the face-swap job, and saves the final video to the requested output folder.

output_examples.input: A remote video URL and remote face image URL are provided for HD output.
output_examples.output: The assistant downloads approved sources, estimates the higher HD credit cost, uploads media, and reports the finished result location.

best_practices: Use only media where you have consent and clear usage rights.
Set VERGING_API_KEY in a private environment before starting a session.
Clean temporary media files after each job finishes.
anti_patterns: Do not use private, copyrighted, or personal media without permission.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts, screenshots, or shared logs.
Do not process unknown URLs unless you trust the source and content.

faq.question: Does this skill run locally?
faq.answer: It runs local helper commands, but face-swap processing happens through the verging.ai API.

faq.question: What API key is required?
faq.answer: The skill expects VERGING_API_KEY from a verging.ai account with enough credits.

faq.question: Can it use YouTube or Bilibili videos?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses yt-dlp to download supported video URLs before trimming and upload.

faq.question: What is the maximum video length?
faq.answer: The documented workflow limits face-swap input to 30 seconds and trims longer videos.

faq.question: Does HD mode cost more?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documentation states HD mode costs three credits per second.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm consent, rights, API credits, installed tools, and whether third-party media upload is acceptable.
